title: CON cache forced eviction wastes OSCORE sequence numbers
description:
In channel.py lines 1179-1208 (_stage_con), when _protected_cons reaches MAX_PROTECTED_CONS (4096) and all entries have active correlation state, the code force-evicts the oldest entry anyway (lines 1200-1204).

This causes legitimate CON retransmissions to be re-protected with new OSCORE sequence numbers instead of reusing the cached protected message, wasting limited sender sequence space.

Failure scenario: Under sustained load with many concurrent CON exchanges:
1. _protected_cons fills to 4096 entries, all with active correlations
2. New CON message triggers eviction of an active entry
3. When that evicted CON retransmits, it cannot find cached protected bytes
4. Re-protection consumes a new sequence number
5. With enough retransmits under pressure, sequence space depletes faster than necessary

Impact: Premature sequence exhaustion requires context re-establishment via EDHOC.

Suggested fix: Increase MAX_PROTECTED_CONS or implement smarter eviction (e.g., prefer evicting entries closest to exchange timeout).

File: src/lichen/coap/secure/channel.py
Lines: 1179-1208
